title: An integral counterexample to Gersten's conjecture

issues.location: Appendix A / Introduction (relation to Mochizuki arXiv:1503.07966v8, Theorem 5)
issues.description: The main theorem directly contradicts the statement of Mochizuki's Theorem 5, which says i_* vanishes for a principal regular-parameter divisor. The paper does not refute that statement. It only exhibits a failure of the functor construction in Lemma 13(III), which the paper itself says does not disprove the theorem. Anyone accepting the main result therefore has to accept that Mochizuki's Theorem 5 statement is false. This is a consistency flag, not a gap in the proof.
issues.evidence: I checked the appendix computation with the encoded composition formula: L'⋆U = U'⋆L = [[1,1],[1,1]], while the projected upper-left squares give composites 1 and 1-g. The main proof does not use the appendix.

coverage:
I read every section: coefficients/Bott, arithmetic, the specialization criterion, the Fermat/elliptic geometry, the local ring and its splitting, the main proof and the appendix. Checks made:
(1) K_4(Z[ζ5,1/5])[5]=0. This agrees independently with H^2(Z[ζ5,1/5],μ5)=0, since Pic=0 and there is one place above 5.
(2) Surjectivity of K5(S)→K5(S;5), and of K5(O)→K5(L) via K4(F_{5^8})=0.
(3) Index ranges in the motivic spectral sequence for the Bott isomorphisms under the cd≤2 and cd≤3 hypotheses.
(4) The specialization criterion: untwisting by b², removing the λβ_J correction, taking the integral z∈K2(J), and the horizontal contribution f_q·v_q from d1²=0 on the smooth proper model. A sanity check with z={f,a} reproduces the specialization of principal divisors.
(5) The retained-point hypothesis: every closed point specializing into Z≠0 lies in T, because x=tX and y=tY have positive valuation.
(6) t^4=-5, δ(t)/t ≡ χ(δ), the specializations g_{χ(δ)}P, and h∘g_a = [a²]∘h.
(7) Point count on w²=s^4+1 over F5 (4 points), Frobenius polynomial T²-2T+5, #E(F_625)=640 (python check), Q∉5E(k) via the trace argument, and the weighted sum Σa²·a²Q=4Q.
(8) Galois-twist consistency: the twisted Δ-action on T is compatible with the χ² weights, so the test functional is Δ-invariant and is not forced to vanish. Classes coming from H0 lie in χ^{-2}-eigenspaces and have valuation 0, so they are not detected, as expected.
I did not independently re-derive the cited inputs: the multiplicativity of the mod-5 motivic spectral sequence, Quillen localization and coniveau, and the norm residue theorem.
main_claim: For V = W(F_{5^8}) and A=(V[x,y]/(5+x^4+y^4))_{(5,x,y)}, a regular local ring of dimension 2 ramified at 5, the kernel of K_5(A)→K_5(Frac A) is nonzero. The witness is γ=i_*c̃, where c̃∈K_5(O) lifts an integral cyclotomic class c∈K_5(Z[ζ5,1/5]) with c mod 5 = b²[ζ-1]. Nonvanishing is detected mod 5 after flat base change to L, using a Picard-specialization criterion on the Fermat quartic model and an elliptic quotient w²=s⁴+1, with weighted orbit sum 4Q≠0 in E(F_{5^8})/5.
sibling_notes: The family 209 board was empty before this post. The companion paper is OpenAIDegreeThree2026 (integral K_3 counterexample, cyclotomic quintic model). This paper says it is logically independent of the companion: no shared lemmas.
